content.value_statement: Canton Network work spans DAML SDK, Canton, and Splice repositories with version rules that are easy to miss. This skill gives concise maps, file pointers, build commands, and LF upgrade checks for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Maps Splice, Canton, and DAML SDK version relationships.
Lists key files for LF versions, compiler targets, and package settings.
Explains package ID inputs and why LF changes alter package hashes.
Provides community Canton and Splice build command references.
Outlines steps for upgrading Splice projects to LF 2.2.
Points to release, documentation, and governance references.
limitations: Does not clone, inspect, or modify repositories by itself.
Version mapping can become stale when upstream projects release new versions.
Does not replace official Canton, DAML, or Splice release notes.
Command execution still requires explicit user or agent action.

use_cases.title: Map repository dependencies
use_cases.description: Understand how Splice, Canton, and DAML SDK versions relate before changing a project.

use_cases.title: Prepare LF target changes
use_cases.description: Find the files and settings that control Daml-LF targets and package compatibility.

use_cases.title: Diagnose build and package issues
use_cases.description: Use documented checks to reason about package ID mismatches and unsupported LF versions.

prompt_templates.title: Map the repositories
prompt_templates.scenario: A new contributor needs the repository hierarchy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the canton-network-repos skill to explain how Splice, Canton, and DAML SDK versions relate for my project.

prompt_templates.title: Find LF configuration files
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is preparing a focused LF configuration review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to list the files I should inspect before changing the Daml-LF target in a Splice repository.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot package IDs
prompt_templates.scenario: A build produced package IDs that do not match expected values.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to diagnose a package ID mismatch after a DAML rebuild. Ask before running commands or editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an LF upgrade
prompt_templates.scenario: A team is planning a cross-repository LF target upgrade.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft an LF 2.2 upgrade plan for Splice based on SDK 3.4.9. Include validation steps and compatibility risks.

output_examples.input: Explain why package IDs changed after changing the LF target.
output_examples.output: The response identifies LF target, SDK version, source content, standard library, and dependencies as package ID inputs. It then lists checks to compare build settings.

output: Files to inspect before the change.
Version settings that must stay aligned.
Build and validation steps to run after user approval.

output_examples.input: Compare enterprise and community Canton deployment features.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes transaction processing, database support, high availability, and pruning differences.

best_practices: Confirm repository versions before applying the version mapping.
Ask for user approval before running build or archive inspection commands.
Cross-check upgrade plans against official release notes before implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not assume package IDs stay stable after changing LF targets.
Do not mix enterprise and community DARs without checking LF compatibility.
Do not treat the embedded version table as a live release feed.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with Canton Network repository mapping, LF version settings, package IDs, and build troubleshooting.

faq.question: Does it run repository commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands and checks, but command execution requires explicit user or agent action.

faq.question: Can it verify the latest Canton release?
faq.answer: No. It points to release references, but current versions must be verified against official sources.

faq.question: Is it only for LF 2.2 work?
faq.answer: No. It includes LF 2.2 guidance and also explains general version and package ID relationships.

faq.question: Can it replace official documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a concise workflow aid and should be checked against official Canton, DAML, and Splice documentation.

faq.question: Which AI tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
